name: Akai MPC Sample
note: Ports from Akai's guide. The MIDI name to match is a guess until `amidi -l` has been run with it plugged into the Pi; its USB id is not captured. Port labels are descriptions, not panel markings, until they are read off the unit.

ports.label: PHONES
ports.about: Headphone output. Plugging in headphones switches the built-in speaker off.

ports.label: MIDI IN
ports.about: MIDI into the MPC: clock, Start and Stop, and notes that play its pads. A setting picks the two TRS jacks or USB.

ports.label: MIDI OUT
ports.about: MIDI from the MPC: pad notes, with Pad MIDI Out set to Always. A setting picks the two TRS jacks or USB.

ports.label: SYNC OUT
ports.about: 3.5 mm TS: a 5 V clock pulse for modular gear.

ports.label: USB-C
ports.about: One port for power, MIDI, a 2-channel audio interface and SD card access. Whether its own output reaches the host is not confirmed.

hardware.extending: Nothing here has been tried on a Pi; how the MPC behaves on Linux is the first thing to settle. To activate it: confirm the MIDI port name with `amidi -l` and fix match.midi, capture the pad note map with `aseqdump` and add it under hardware.midi.pad_note_map. A pad map is what lets a virtual 4x4 bank line up with the real pads. Everything under "hardware" is ignored by the Go loader: it is notes for people, and for a later registry (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-device-profiles-design.md). To fill this profile from a real unit, follow 'Capturing an unknown device' in docs/hardware/README.md, then flip statuses from 'unconfirmed' or 'to-capture' to 'owner'.

connection.note: Plays through the Sidekick, usually channel 2. Plugging it into the Pi over USB is being considered; the single USB-C port is shared by power, MIDI, audio and the SD card.

usb_output_to_host.$comment: Whether the MPC's own output reaches the host over USB is not documented.

midi.one_active_port_at_a_time: The MIDI port setting picks the two TRS jacks or USB.
midi.sync_out_pulse: 3.5 mm TS, 5 V clock pulse for modular gear

pad_note_map.$comment: Not published. MPCs usually start at note 36. Capture it with aseqdump while hitting pads 1-16.

storage.internal: 8 GB, 2 GB of it factory content
storage.card: microSD; Project > SD Card Access mounts it as a drive over USB

layout.$comment: From owner reports on MPC-Forums, not a maker document.

project_format.note: .xpj, reported as gzip-compressed JSON by a third-party converter; reverse-engineered, not documented by Akai.

controls.fader: 1; pad volume by default, assignable with SHIFT + PAD 9

quirks.text: One USB-C port carries power, MIDI, audio and SD card access. SD Card Access is a mode picked on the device; MIDI over USB is probably unavailable while it is on.
Akai lists Mac, Windows, iOS and Android as hosts, not Linux.
Battery powered; charging may only work with the unit off, depending on cable and source (5 V / 2 A recommended).

unknowns.question: Does it appear as a MIDI device on the Pi with the MIDI port set to USB?
Does it appear as an audio device, and with how many channels in and out?
USB vendor and product ids, in each mode
unknowns.how: lsusb, once normally and once with Project > SD Card Access on

unknowns.question: Does the SD card mount on the Pi in SD Card Access mode?
unknowns.how: lsblk after switching the mode on; copy a WAV into MPC-Sample/Samples/User/ and check the MPC sees it

unknowns.question: Does a sequence follow MIDI clock from the Pi?
unknowns.how: Sync in = MIDI Clock on the MPC, then send clock from the Pi

hindsight.role: One-shot and finger-drumming instrument. Notes are made on it; its audio is caught by Hindsight through the Sidekick.
notes: Direction under discussion: assign clips to pads on a virtual MPC in Hindsight, and carry the bank to the real MPC as a kit on its card (the MPC then plays them itself).
Needs the pad note map above before a virtual bank can line up with the real pads.
